title: Continuity of Hom out of $C$ is closed under extensions and shifts
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\Lambda$ a condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. Put $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and let $\mathcal T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X})=D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ be the ordinary unbounded derived category of sheaves of left $\Lambda_X$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with its shifts and distinguished triangles [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Let $I$ be a small filtered category and $(K_i^\bullet)_{i\in I}$ a diagram of complexes of these modules. Let $K^\bullet=\varinjlim_i K_i^\bullet$ be its termwise colimit, with structure maps $\kappa_i:K_i^\bullet\to K^\bullet$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Write $K_i,K$ for their images in $\mathcal T$. No common lower bound is required for this formal assertion.

For $C\in\mathcal T$ and $q\in\mathbf Z$ let
$$
\theta_{C,q}:\varinjlim_i\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(C,K_i[q])\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(C,K[q]),\qquad [h_i]\longmapsto\kappa_i[q]\circ h_i,
$$
where the colimit is in abelian groups. Let $\mathcal C$ consist of those $C$ for which $\theta_{C,q}$ is bijective for every $q$. Then $\mathcal C$ is closed under shifts, isomorphisms and extensions: if $C'\to C\to C''\to C'[1]$ is distinguished and $C',C''\in\mathcal C$, then $C\in\mathcal C$. More generally, any finite construction by extensions, shifts and isomorphisms from any collection $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal C$ stays in $\mathcal C$. This applies in particular to any supplied family of objects $a_!L$ satisfying the comparison condition.

For the constructible specialization, assume in addition that $X$ is Noetherian, meaning locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and a finite intermediate extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Take $\Lambda=\underline E$ or $\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$ with the condensed coefficient conventions [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Here $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ means bounded complexes with constructible cohomology in the finite constant local model sense of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Here a locally closed immersion $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ is a composite $a=i\circ u$ with $u:S\hookrightarrow Z$ an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For such a factorization put $a_!L=i_*u_!L$ using module pushforward [def-sfb-module-lower-star] and open extension by zero [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek]. A lisse $\Lambda_S$-module means a module locally isomorphic for the pro-étale topology to a finite direct sum of $\Lambda_S$. If every such $a_!L$ lies in $\mathcal C$, then every object of $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ lies in $\mathcal C$.

proof.text: For every $C,q$ the maps $h\mapsto\kappa_i[q]\circ h$ are additive and compatible with the transition maps, since $\kappa_j\circ K(\alpha)=\kappa_i$ for $\alpha:i\to j$. The colimit universal property gives the stated $\theta_{C,q}$. A shift is an additive equivalence, so applying $[-n]$ gives natural additive bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(C[n],K_i[q])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(C,K_i[q+(-n)])$ and the analogous bijection for $K$. Their inverses apply $[n]$. They commute with postcomposition by $\kappa_i[q]$, hence identify $\theta_{C[n],q}$ with $\theta_{C,q-n}$. This proves shift closure. If $e:D\xrightarrow{\sim}C$, precomposition with $e$ and $e^{-1}$ gives inverse additive bijections of the two Hom diagrams and their targets, commuting with $\theta$, so isomorphism closure follows. Also $0\in\mathcal C$, since every Hom group out of $0$ is zero.

source.place: Shifts paragraph; definition of the comparison map

proof.text:
Write the given distinguished triangle as $C'\xrightarrow{u}C\xrightarrow{v}C''\xrightarrow{w}C'[1]$. For any $W\in\mathcal T$ form the five-term row
$$\operatorname{Hom}(C'[1],W)\xrightarrow{w^*}\operatorname{Hom}(C'',W)\xrightarrow{v^*}\operatorname{Hom}(C,W)\xrightarrow{u^*}\operatorname{Hom}(C',W)\xrightarrow{(-w[-1])^*}\operatorname{Hom}(C''[-1],W).$$
Here $t^*(h)=h\circ t$, with the usual shift identifications. Clause (ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact] gives exactness at the second term and clause (i) gives it at the third. Apply clause (i) to the inverse-rotated distinguished triangle $C''[-1]\xrightarrow{-w[-1]}C'\xrightarrow{u}C\xrightarrow{v}C''$ to obtain exactness at the fourth term. Its rotation has arrows $u,v,-(-w[-1])[1]=w$, under the shift identifications, so TR2 gives precisely the original triangle and proves that this inverse rotation is distinguished. Clause (i) of [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact], applied also to rotations, says that the consecutive triangle composites vanish; hence each consecutive pair in this Hom row has zero composite, as required for exactness. All three uses are for a pre-triangulated category and an arbitrary $W$; there is no boundedness condition.

Fix $q$. Apply the row of step 2 to $W=K_i[q]$ for every $i$ and to $W=K[q]$. Every horizontal arrow is precomposition with a fixed arrow $t$ in the triangle or its inverse rotation. Postcomposition with any transition map commutes with it by associativity. The same calculation with the cocone maps gives
$$\theta_{A,q}([h_i\circ t])=\kappa_i[q]\circ h_i\circ t=\theta_{B,q}([h_i])\circ t$$
for $t:A\to B$. This includes $t=-w[-1]$, by additivity. Thus these are diagrams of exact rows and the five comparison maps give a commutative ladder. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact], taking the colimit over the small filtered category $I$ leaves the first row exact at its three inner terms. The target row is exact by step 2. All colimits in this step are of abelian groups, not colimits in the derived category.

source.place: Tag 00DB, lemma-directed-colimit-exact; applied spotwise to the Hom rows of Tag 0149

proof.text: Suppose $C',C''\in\mathcal C$. By step 1, $C'[1]$ and $C''[-1]$ also belong to $\mathcal C$. Consequently the first, second, fourth and fifth vertical arrows in the ladder of step 3 are bijective homomorphisms of abelian groups, hence isomorphisms. In particular the first is epic and the fifth is monic. The rows are exact at the three inner terms, so [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma], with $\mathcal A=\mathrm{Ab}$, makes the middle vertical arrow $\theta_{C,q}$ an isomorphism. Since $q$ was arbitrary, $C\in\mathcal C$.

source.place: Tag 05QB, lemma-five-lemma, applied to the five-term Hom ladder

proof.text: Let a finite construction start with objects of $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal C$ (and, if allowed, $0$). Induct on its number of operations. The starting objects and $0$ lie in $\mathcal C$. A shift or an isomorphic replacement stays in $\mathcal C$ by step 1, and an extension stays in it by step 4. This proves the finite-construction assertion. For later use it also gives closure under cones: if $A\to B\to D\to A[1]$ is distinguished and $A,B\in\mathcal C$, its rotation $B\to D\to A[1]\to B[1]$ is distinguished. Shift closure puts $A[1]$ in $\mathcal C$, and extension closure then puts $D$ in $\mathcal C$. The minus sign in the rotated final arrow does not affect which vertices belong to the class.

source.place: The consequence paragraph: induction along the finite construction, with cones reduced to extensions by rotation

proof.text: Now impose the hypotheses of the constructible specialization. They are exactly the Noetherian-scheme and field-coefficient hypotheses of [det-cor-coefficient-heart-ii-generation]. That node says that every $M\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ has a finite witness whose entries are $a_!L[n]$ or cones of morphisms between earlier entries, up to shifts and isomorphisms. Each generator there is $a_!L[n]$ with $a_!L=i_*u_!L$ formed through the factorization $a=i\circ u$ of the locally closed immersion through the closure of its image, $u$ open and $i$ closed, and with $L$ locally free of finite rank for the pro-étale topology. That factorization is one of the open-then-closed factorizations admitted in our hypothesis and $L$ is lisse in our sense (locally isomorphic to a finite direct sum of $\Lambda_S$), so the assumed membership gives $a_!L\in\mathcal C$, and step 1 puts every $a_!L[n]$ in $\mathcal C$. Induct along the witness: an entry in the generating class lies in $\mathcal C$ as just shown; an entry isomorphic to $\operatorname{Cone}(f)[m]$ for a morphism $f$ between earlier entries lies in $\mathcal C$ by the cone closure of step 5, followed by the shift and isomorphism closure of step 1. Hence the last object $M$ lies in $\mathcal C$. This includes the zero and empty-scheme cases. Only the finite constant local model constructibility occurring in the cited generation theorem is used; there is no identification with an arbitrary ring-object local finite presentation predicate.
